app.title: Plant Species Occurrence Dashboard
app.summary: The dashboard loads a collection of species occurrence records that a fetch-and-clean pipeline has already prepared. In a sidebar, the person narrows the records by species, family, state and country, and limits them to a range of collection years. Headline counts, a map of the records whose coordinates are trustworthy, and bar charts by family, state, country and year all update to the current subset. The person can then read the filtered records in a table and download them as a CSV.

task.text: Explore a cleaned collection of species occurrence records by taxon, place and collection year: see where they fall on a map, how they break down by category, and export the subset of interest.

data.text: A table of occurrence records gathered from a biodiversity records network. Each record has a scientific name, family, standardised country and state, collection year, decimal coordinates and a flag saying whether its coordinate passed cleaning.
data.item: one occurrence record of a species at a place and year

stage.text: exploring occurrence records after fetching and cleaning, before analysis

mechanism.text: Sidebar multiselects and a year-range slider filter one shared subset of records, and every other view redraws from it: headline numbers, a species-coloured point or density map of records with valid coordinates, top-category bar charts, and a records table with CSV download. The map can be switched between two map engines, and between points and a density heatmap.

field.text: species occurrence records and coordinate cleaning in biodiversity informatics

workflow.name: filter located records by category and period, summarize, map and export the subset

steps.here: The combined per-species record files from the bundled dataset are loaded and cached. If there are none, the dashboard says to run the fetch command first.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Multiselects for species, family, standardised state and standardised country narrow the records. An empty selection means no filter.
A range slider, bounded by the cleaned collection years, keeps records inside the range. Records with no year are kept.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Three headline numbers for the subset: the record count, the species count, and the percent georeferenced (the share of records whose coordinate passed cleaning).
Records with a valid coordinate are drawn on a map. A radio button switches between a species-coloured point map with an optional density heatmap and a map with clustered circle markers.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Bar charts count records for the top 15 families, states and countries, and for each year, using every filtered record.
The filtered records are shown in a table and can be downloaded as a CSV file of occurrences.

distinctive: Only records whose coordinate passed cleaning are drawn on the map (numeric, in range, not 0,0, on land, not a per-species distance outlier). Counts, charts, the table and the export still include every record.
Percent georeferenced is computed from the coordinate-validity flag, so the headline number and the map agree on which records count as located.
The state and country filters use standardised names, with states written as 'State (Country)', so abbreviations and spelling variants collapse into one entry.
Points on the map are coloured by species, with distinct colours for the most frequent species and one grey for the rest.
